blocks.userQuestion: When do I have to give my documents to the other side and to the court?
blocks.whatsHappening: You must serve and file documents before certain events. At least 14 days before the settlement conference, serve on every other party and file with the court any document you will rely on at trial. This includes expert reports not attached to your claim or defence. You must also serve and file a list of proposed witnesses on Form 13A. At least 30 days before the trial, serve any document or record you want in evidence on all parties served with the notice of trial. These documents will be received in evidence unless the judge orders otherwise.
blocks.whatToDoNext: Serve and file your documents as required. Use personal service or an alternative method allowed by the rules. Make notes of the service details for your affidavit of service.
blocks.whatHappensAfter: Once served and filed, your documents may be used in court. If served 30 days before trial, they will be received in evidence unless the judge decides otherwise.

citations.quote: At least 14 days before the date of the settlement conference, each party shall serve on every other party and file with the court,
a copy of any document to be relied on at the trial, including an expert report, not attached to the party's claim or defence
a list of proposed witnesses (Form 13A) and of other persons with knowledge of the matters in dispute in the action

A document or written statement or an audio or visual record that has been served, at least 30 days before the trial date, on all parties who were served with the notice of trial, shall be received in evidence, unless the trial judge orders otherwise.
A party who serves on another party a written statement or document described in subrule (2) shall append to or include in the statement or document,
A party who has been served with a written statement or document described in subrule (2) and wishes to cross-examine the witness or author may summon him or her as a witness under subrule 18.03 (1).

definedAt.quote: A settlement conference shall be held in every defended action.

readabilityException.justification: The name of a specific proceeding the Rules require and fix a date for. "Meeting" or "hearing" would be inaccurate: a settlement conference is neither a trial nor an informal meeting, it is the event r. 13.03 (2) counts 14 days back from, and a reader told to serve documents before a "meeting" cannot identify which event that is on their notice from the court.
